newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE-Pakistan fuel oil refinery on track - paper.
newsitem.headline: UAE-Pakistan fuel oil refinery on track - paper.

text.p: Pakistan's State Petroleum and Marketing Co (Perac) and Sharjah-based Crescent Petroleum Co have resumed talks on a $650 million oil hydrocracker project, the UAE newspaper Khaleej Times reported on Monday.

"The new Pakistani government is learnt to have issued a letter earlier this month for the revival of the project. This follows a fence-mending process conducted by the two partners," the newspaper reported.

Perac told Crescent in July 1996 that it was unilaterally ending its 1993 agreement with Crescent Refining and Marketing Co to develop the hydrocracker in Karachi after parties differed over the project's rate of return.
The hydrocracker will have the capacity to convert 1.65 million tonnes a year of fuel oil supplied from two local refineries into products, mostly high speed diesel.
Products would be sold in the local market
"Negotiations on the right incentive package for the implementation of the project are still going on and it might take another month for both parties to come to an agreement," the paper reported.
